[EFFECT]
The hour of day has a strongly non-monotonic, double-peaked effect on predicted demand. Contributions are most negative in the pre-dawn hours (roughly 3–5 a.m., where the model predicts the fewest rentals), then rise sharply through the morning to a first peak around 7–8 a.m. Demand then dips slightly through midday before climbing again to the highest peak of the day at around 5–6 p.m. (hours 17–18), after which contributions fall steadily through the late evening.

[IMPORTANCE]
Hour of day is by far the most important feature in the model, ranked **1st out of 9** with an importance score of **0.83** — more than four times larger than the second-ranked feature (year, at 0.20). It dominates the model's predictions.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan bike availability and staffing around two daily demand surges — a morning peak (around 7–8 a.m.) and a larger evening peak (around 5–6 p.m.) — and reduce resources during the early morning hours (roughly 3–5 a.m.) when demand is at its lowest.
